source.title: Massively Distributed SGD: ImageNet/ResNet-50 Training in a Flash
source.authors: Hiroaki Mikami; Hisahiro Suganuma; Pongsakorn U-chupala; Yoshiki Tanaka; Yuichi Kageyama

record.tranche_reason: Tests the large-batch generalization claim on ImageNet/ResNet-50 using validation accuracy under batch-size control and label smoothing; it does not reproduce the fixed-epoch comparisons in the claim version.
record.gate_note: The authors report five experimental setups with validation accuracy and batch-size conditions. Table 1 values for prior work are cited comparisons, not rows.
record.test_reason: The study's own ImageNet/ResNet-50 experiments test V5's adapted-recipe qualification: larger batches retain validation accuracy near a 32K reference. Table 3 specifies 90-epoch training, contrary to the record's claim that fixed-epoch comparisons are absent. There is no matched small-batch or unadapted large-batch control, and learning-rate configurations also vary.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate. The authors report that batch-size control or label smoothing enables very large-batch training with little accuracy loss, while combining them in Exp. 3 lowers accuracy by about 0.7 percentage points. Their headline result is 75.29% validation accuracy in 122 seconds using 3456 GPUs.
record.recipe_differences: ImageNet/ResNet-50 large-batch training with batch-size control and label smoothing; does not use the fixed-epoch comparisons described in V5.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported accuracy differs between batch-size control alone, label smoothing alone, and their combination.
record.problems: The study does not report a fixed-epoch comparison or a small-batch run matched to the experimental recipes. It reports validation accuracy but no uncertainty estimates.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-versus-random-label held-out performance.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets.
The unadapted large-batch penalty relative to matched small-batch training; the workload-dependent threshold; longer-training remedies; language models; isolated causal effects of each recipe change.
Measured magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V5. Its 90-epoch comparisons bear on recipe adaptation, but the 32K reference is itself large-batch training. No uncertainty estimates or formal significance tests are reported; descriptions of insignificant loss are the authors' assessments.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and test performance on natural versus random labels.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers compared with SGD or momentum SGD.
Fixed-epoch comparisons; language models; broader batch-size ranges without batch-size control or label smoothing; normalization or regularization changes beyond those reported.
Dropout and its interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Sharpness or other measured network properties associated with the generalization gap.
Removal of memorized examples and resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Reference training setup; validation accuracy reported.
rows.note: Reference result; the text does not identify it as a fixed-epoch comparison.
rows.check: Valid own-experiment reference, but its accuracy alone cannot establish a batch-size penalty. Add the 90-epoch budget from Table 3; batch-size control and label smoothing are absent.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.note: Authors say batch-size control enables large mini-batch training with no significant accuracy loss.
rows.check: Accuracy is 0.37 percentage points below the 32K reference. The text does not explicitly declare Exp. 1's difference insignificant. Add the 90-epoch budget, absence of label smoothing, and the footnote that this experiment used an earlier software version. Recipe differences prevent attributing the difference solely to batch size.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.note: Authors say label smoothing permits an initial mini-batch size up to 54K with no significant accuracy loss.
rows.check: For the batch-size penalty, the authors explicitly report no significant accuracy loss: 75.29% versus 75.40%. The original observed state reverses the meaning of the measured effect. Add the 90-epoch budget and absence of batch-size control.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Combined batch-size control and label smoothing.
rows.note: Authors state that combining the techniques with large mini-batch size decreases accuracy by about 0.7%.
rows.check: The penalty is clearly present: 74.62% versus 75.40%, a 0.78-percentage-point decrease, described by the authors as about 0.7%. V5 specifies no larger minimum effect that would justify partial. Add the 90-epoch budget; recipe differences limit causal attribution.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.note: Authors state that batch-size control alone enables a maximum mini-batch size up to 119K with no significant accuracy loss.
rows.check: The authors explicitly report no significant accuracy loss: 75.23% versus 75.40%. The original observed state reverses the meaning of the batch-size penalty. Add the 90-epoch budget and absence of label smoothing; 119K is the maximum scheduled batch size.

relationships.condition: Label smoothing at 54K, or scheduled batch-size control from 34K to 119K, over 90 epochs
relationships.reason: R3 and R5 support the adapted-recipe qualification: accuracies of 75.29% and 75.23% remain near the 75.40% reference, with no significant loss according to the authors.
relationships.display_finding: The study's results suggest label smoothing and scheduled batch growth retained accuracy near the reference. These results have not been verified.

relationships.condition: Scheduled batches of 34K/68K, and combined label smoothing with 54K/64K batches
relationships.reason: R2 and R4 show that these adaptations do not uniformly preserve reference accuracy: losses are 0.37 and 0.78 percentage points; differing recipes prevent isolating batch size as the cause.
relationships.display_finding: The study reports residual accuracy deficits under the adapted large-batch recipes, but the comparisons remain unverified and differing recipes prevent isolating batch size.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Batch-size control alone or label smoothing alone on ImageNet/ResNet-50
reader_labels.reason: Large batches achieved validation accuracy near the 32K reference; R2, R3 and R5.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Combining batch-size control and label smoothing at 54K/64K
